newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope makes new call for peace in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Pope makes new call for peace in Northern Ireland.

text.p: Pope John Paul made a fresh plea on Sunday for an end to the conflict in Northern Ireland, saying "nothing is lost through peace (but) everything can be lost through violence".
"Let us all pray that the Irish people will put tension and conflict behind them and go on to build a brighter and more serene future for the younger generation," the Pope said.
"Nothing is lost through peace; everything can be lost through violence," he said.
He made his remarks in his noon address to pilgrims gathered in St Peter's Square for a beatification service that put an Irish Catholic, Edmund Ignatius Rice, on the road to sainthood.

The Pope asked pilgrims to pray that the Christian heritage of the Irish people "will be the inspiration of new harmony and peace between the communities of Northern Ireland, between people of different political views".

A two-year-old peace process for the British-ruled province launched by the governments of Britain and Ireland is under assault from both pro-Ireland Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas and pro-British Protestant militia.
The Pope's beatification service, for 16 Roman Catholics, was his last public ceremony before he enters hospital in Rome later on Sunday for an operation to remove his appendix.
Rice, who lived from 1762 to 1844, was a wealthy landowner and merchant at a time when all of predominantly Catholic Ireland was under British rule.
Rice opened a school for poor children and founded the Congregation of Christian Brothers, a teaching order which is now spread throughout the world.
